subject: general
question:
Which of the following is a displacement reaction?

(i) ZncO₃ (s) → ZnO (s) + CO₂ (g)

(ii) Fe (s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s)

(iii) 2H₂ (g) + O₂ (g) →2H2O(I)

(v) CaCO₃ (s) →CaO(s) + CO₂ (g)
solution:
The correct answer is__** (ii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A displacement reaction is a type of chemical reaction.**
 
• In a displacement reaction, **one element is replaced by another element in a compound.**
 
• The more reactive element **"displaces**" the less reactive element from the compound.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the reaction **Fe (s) CuSO4(aq) → FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s), Fe (Iron)** is the replacing element and **Cu (Copper)** is the replaced element.
 
• The iron ion** (Fe2+) is oxidized to Fe3+ in the process**, and the **copper ion (Cu2+) is reduced to Cu metal.**
 
• The reaction between **Fe and CuSO4 can be used to extract copper from copper-containing ores**
 
• The reaction is an example of single replacement reaction or single displacement reaction.
 
• This reaction is also an** oxidation-reduction reaction**, as the oxidation state of Iron changes from** 0 to +3 and Copper changes from +2 to 0.**
 
• The reaction is exothermic and releases heat.
 
• The reaction typically proceeds in the presence of a suitable** oxidizing agent, such as H2SO4 or HNO3**, which helps to oxidize the iron.
